simple.meaning: חָלָא (châlâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be sick.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 2 Chronicles, beginning at 2 Chronicles 16:12. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָלָא (H2456) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָלָא (châlâʼ) / H2456 is traced through 2 Chronicles 16:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2456. chala I. [ חָלָא ] verb be sick, diseased (= חלה , see Ges § 75 , 22) — Qal Imperfect אָסָאבְּ֗֗֗רַגְלָיו וַיֶּחֱלֶא 2Chr 16:12 (= חלה 1Kin 15:23 ).

occurrences.englishText: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa was diseased in his feet. His disease was exceedingly great: yet in his disease he didn’t seek Yahweh, but just the physicians.
